tracks.legalName: Consolidated Petition to Seal More Than One Record in District Court (NRS 179.2595)
tracks.note: Drafted controlled pleading with proposed order. The affidavit/declaration in support and the prosecutor stipulation are required packet components but are recorded as a dependency rather than drafted: the stipulation records the prosecuting agency's position and neither instrument's text is committed.

tracks.legalName: Removal of a Record from the Central Repository After a Favourable Disposition (NRS 179A.160)
tracks.note: Not a filing route. NRS 179A.160 is a written application to the Central Repository and the record-holding agency; no court, no order, no proposed order. Rendering a court pleading would fabricate a proceeding the statute does not create. Ledger classifies the track as custom_pleading; the committed evidence contradicts that classification and the contradiction is recorded, not resolved by drafting.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of Records After Decriminalization of an Offence (NRS 179.271)
tracks.note: Governing mechanism unread. The full text of NRS 179.271 was never obtained; only the chapter-index heading is committed. Whether the instrument is a written request or a full petition is unresolved, so the filing vehicle itself is unsettled.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of Records After an Unconditional Pardon (NRS 179.273)
tracks.note: Governing mechanism unread, and the primary remedy is automatic sealing. The full text of NRS 179.273 was never obtained. Offering a petition as the default output would push a participant into a filing they may not need.
